requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

The enlarged hardware depicts the supplied matte-charcoal forms: a flat rounded-rectangle R1 pull with proportions corresponding to 24 × 8 mm, 2 mm corner radii, an upper centered 12 × 3 mm attachment slot and centered R1 engraving below it; and a rectangular three-bar ladder-lock buckle corresponding to 35 × 30 mm for 25 mm webbing. Perspective and rendering style may vary. A different pull outline, missing slot or engraving, or a different buckle mechanism fails; physical dimensions need not be inferred precisely from pixels.

The views collectively establish a vest that fits beneath the shell and overtrousers with shaped knee articulation and separate left and right ankle buckle adjustments. Visible garment records also agree with the fixed hood and center-front shell zipper, sleeveless center-front zipped vest and elastic trouser waistband. Hidden features need not be visible in every pose; a contradictory construction or absent required feature across the evidence fails.

A, B and C are identifiable alternatives, each presenting CW01, CW02 and CW03 with assessable silhouettes, panel arrangements and color placement. There must be meaningful wardrobe-design differences between the directions; merely changing the board title or rearranging identical drawings fails. Silhouette and panel choices remain open within the fixed garment requirements.

The process establishes A, B and C before a single direction is selected. The selection explains handlebar reach, pocket access and walking; the materials, fit and range documents develop that same choice, and the presentation's opening page states its letter. Organization may vary, but contradictory selections, missing functional reasons or development of a different alternative fail. Image and video continuity are assessed separately.

Both specification documents assign the shell and overtrousers to F01 and the vest to F02. The materials sheet records F01 as 125 g/m² total, 1450 mm wide, a 2.5-layer laminate with a 100% nylon 40-denier plain-weave face, polyurethane membrane, printed inner protective layer and matte water-repellent face; F02 is 100% polyester, 180 g/m², 1500 mm wide, warp-knitted tricot with brushed inner and smooth outer faces. Moss #465B57 is dominant; Clay #B86E50 may be used for panels and trims, and hardware is matte charcoal. The presentation repeats COMMON WEATHER, each style/fabric pairing and Moss #465B57. Equivalent units and tabular or prose records are acceptable; missing fabric properties or conflicting assignments fail.

Three identifiable finished garment crops show CW01/F01, CW02/F02 and CW03/F01, each with its applicable color code. The plate also prints COMMON WEATHER and identifies Moss #465B57 as the main color. Fabric surfaces and color placement agree with the materials sheet and final garments; optional Clay accents retain #B86E50. Crop scale and lighting may vary. A missing style, raw swatches replacing finished crops, wrong codes or contradictory surfaces and color placement fail.

Each document states the M shell's 720 mm front, 800 mm back, 80 mm collar and 690 mm sleeve, plus 80 mm back drop and 30 mm extension over a 660 mm reference. The materials sheet additionally records F01 lockstitch with 10 mm allowance and 20 mm internal tape, F02 overlock with 6 mm allowance, a 24 × 8 mm R1 pull with 2 mm corners and a 12 × 3 mm attachment slot, and a 35 × 30 mm buckle for 25 mm webbing. Equivalent units are acceptable; missing required repetitions, swapped measurements or incorrect seam/hardware records fail.

Each plate independently annotates the size M shell with front length 720 mm, back length 800 mm, collar 80 mm, sleeve 690 mm, back drop 80 mm and sleeve extension 30 mm. The sleeve reference is 660 mm, and leaders or captions associate values with the proper regions and measurement endpoints. The shell retains its fixed hood. Callout style may vary; omission, disagreement with the specification or misleading measurement placement fails.

Every flat-lay image prints COMMON WEATHER and the style/fabric codes for the garments it depicts. Each lineup identifies CW01/F01, CW02/F02 and CW03/F01; individual shell, vest and trouser views identify their respective pair. Typography and placement may vary, but codes must be legible and unambiguously associated with the correct garment. A missing brand, missing relevant code or incorrect assignment fails.

Each front-lineup label enlargement carries both required phrases at the inside back neck of CW01/CW02 or inside back waistband of CW03. Details show R1 engraving, separate buckles at both ankles and zipped pockets enclosing the phone at the chest, gloves at wearer-right and cap at wearer-left, dimensioned 170 × 85 × 12, 220 × 110 × 40 and 180 × 100 × 30 mm respectively. Two outer-cuff tabs are each 60 × 10 mm; the horizontal center-back strip is 120 × 10 mm with its lower edge 100 mm above the hem. Track each garment's seams, pockets and closures across flat and worn views. Documented size grading, perspective and folds may change appearance; label omissions, wrong storage or reflector records, missing ankle hardware or ungraded redesigns fail.

The size note and presentation contain these S/M/L records in mm: CW01 chest 1100/1180/1260, hem 1140/1220/1300, front 700/720/740, back 780/800/820, sleeve 680/690/700, reference sleeve 650/660/670, collar 80/80/80, chest-pocket opening 180/190/200, drop 250/260/270 and offset 80/90/100; CW02 chest 1040/1120/1200, hem 1080/1160/1240 and front/back length 640/660/680; CW03 relaxed waist 720/800/880, extended waist 1000/1080/1160, hip 1080/1160/1240, inseam 750/770/790 and knee position 560/580/600. The size note gives the corresponding per-step increments, full-circumference and measurement-point definitions, M shell chest ease of 180 mm over a 1000 mm reference body, and constants of 80 mm back drop, 30 mm sleeve extension, unchanged reflectors, 100 mm reflector hem offset, hardware and item envelopes. The range plan and presentation identify CW01 Hooded Shell, CW02 Layering Vest and CW03 Overtrousers and all three M combinations: closed shell over vest for cycling, open shell over vest with daypack for trail walking, and shell carried over one arm with vest and trousers worn for café arrival. Equivalent units and reorganized tables are acceptable; missing rows, incorrect grading, names or wearing states fail.

The cycling image labels size S and annotates chest-pocket opening 180 mm, drop 250 mm, offset 80 mm and knee position 560 mm. The trail image labels size L and gives opening 200 mm, drop 270 mm, offset 100 mm and knee position 600 mm. Leaders or clear captions connect these values to the actual pocket and knee articulation, using high shoulder point, center front and top of waistband as the specified origins. Annotation style may vary; size labels alone, swapped values or visibly misplaced details fail.

The lineups each contain all three M styles and the individual flats provide the actual front and back of every style. Worn images cover M cycling, M trail, M café, S cycling and L trail. Cycling shows closed shell over vest, trousers and forward handlebar reach consistent with the riding reference. Trail images show walking with open shell over vest, trousers and a small daypack. Café M shows the shell carried over one arm with vest and trousers worn. Main colors remain consistent with the selected material plan under different lighting. Duplicate views, wrong sides, missing styles, wrong activity/size combinations or incorrect wearing states fail. Video and presentation requirements are assessed by their own checks.

Review the entire 12-second sequence, allowing ordinary frame rounding. One size M wearer performs visible shell-over-vest layering, forward handlebar reach and walking in the overtrousers. Construction, hardware, material colors and fit agree with the selected M wardrobe. Cuts and viewpoint changes are acceptable; a missing action, wearer substitution, changed garment design or materially incorrect duration fails.

requirementChecks.criteria: The presentation has at least ten pages and visibly reuses every listed source: three alternatives, selection, all three specification documents, eight flat-lay images, detail plates and five worn images. Readable excerpts, crops and scaled arrangements are allowed if source identity and required information survive. References by title without reused content, replacement imagery or any omitted source fail.

All eight flats develop the direction identified in the selection note, preserving its garment silhouettes, panel arrangements and color placement. Individual front and back views agree with the corresponding lineup garments in seams, pockets, closures, hardware and garment proportions.

Worn garments and detail crops preserve the final flat-view construction while allowing documented size grading, pose, folds and perspective. Material assignments and Moss and optional Clay placement agree across the specification, finished crops and all five worn outfits. S and L pocket and knee positions follow the size note while hardware, reflective dimensions, hem offset and packed-item envelopes remain constant. The three M wearing states agree with the range plan, including the exposed trail vest and carried café shell.
